Foundation for Women Warriors (FFWW) is a 106-year-old nonprofit organization dedicated to honoring and empowering women veterans and their families. The Program Coordinator serves as a primary point of contact for women veterans seeking support through Foundation for Women Warriors' programs. This position conducts intake assessments, identifies participant needs, coordinates appropriate program services, provides ongoing case oversight, and monitors participant progress toward achieving personal and financial stability. 

The Program Coordinator is responsible for maintaining accurate client records, tracking program outcomes, supporting grant reporting requirements, and ensuring veterans receive high-quality, compassionate service throughout their engagement with the organization.

Veteran Support & Case Oversight

Identify barriers to services and develop strategies to help veterans successfully access available resources. 
Clearly communicate program expectations, eligibility requirements, timelines, and next steps. 
Provide ongoing case oversight through regular follow-up and quarterly check-ins. 
Assist veterans in developing personal budgets, setting financial goals, and improving financial literacy to promote long-term self-sufficiency. 
Support veterans in identifying and securing housing, childcare, and other essential community resources. 
Assist with applications and prepare documentation, including payment or check requests, as needed. 
Review veteran surveys and assessments to identify additional support needs and opportunities for long-term success. 

Program Administration & Data Management

Maintain accurate, timely, and complete case documentation within the organization's client management system. 
Ensure the integrity and confidentiality of client records while complying with organizational policies and funder requirements. 
Collect, monitor, and report program outcomes and grant-required performance metrics using Apricot or other designated databases. 
Conduct periodic audits of client files to ensure documentation accuracy and compliance. 
Collaborate with the team to support reporting, data analysis, and program evaluation. 
Prepare internal and external reports highlighting program activities, outcomes, and impact. 
Review veteran applications for completeness, accuracy, and financial sustainability. 
Maintain reporting calendars and ensure compliance with grant deadlines, reporting requirements, and program deliverables. 

Program Support & Organizational Engagement

Participate in staff meetings, trainings, community events, and professional development opportunities. 
Collaborate with team members on program improvements, special projects, and strategic initiatives. 
Contribute to the ongoing development and refinement of program goals, objectives, and participant services. 
Perform other duties as assigned. 

Qualifications

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

Excellent verbal, written, and interpersonal communication skills. 
Strong organizational skills with exceptional attention to detail. 
Ability to build trusting relationships with veterans while maintaining professional boundaries. 
Strong critical thinking and problem-solving skills. 
Ability to work independently while contributing effectively as part of a collaborative team. 
Experience managing multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment. 
Strong database management and data entry skills. 
Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite and client management software (CRM/database systems). 
Excellent online research skills and ability to connect veterans with appropriate community resources. 
Commitment to maintaining confidentiality and exercising sound professional judgment. 

Education & Experience

Bachelor's degree in Social Work, Human Services, Psychology, Public Administration, or a related field preferred. 
Equivalent combination of education and relevant experience will be considered. 
Experience working with veterans, military families, low-income populations, or other underserved communities preferred. 
Knowledge of community resources, public benefits, and supportive services. 
Demonstrated ability to work effectively with individuals from diverse cultural, socioeconomic, and military backgrounds. 

Additional Requirements

Valid California driver's license. 
Reliable personal vehicle with current automobile insurance. 
Ability to travel locally for client meetings, community events, trainings, and partner meetings. 
Successful completion of Foundation for Women Warriors onboarding and required communication training. 

Our Values

At Foundation for Women Warriors, our mission is driven by integrity, honor, commitment, community, and pursue of excellence. We believe every interaction is an opportunity to empower women veterans and strengthen their path toward long-term stability and success. We value collaboration, accountability, respect, and innovation, and we are committed to creating an inclusive workplace where every team member is encouraged to grow, lead, and make a meaningful impact. Together, we honor the service of women veterans and empower her future by serving them with excellence, dignity, and purpose.

jobs.description:
ASE, an Akima company, is looking to hire a Physical Science Technician who will contribute to multidisciplinary research teams by supporting field data collection, maintaining scientific instrumentation, processing environmental samples, and organizing datasets used for hydrologic and watershed assessments. Work involves routine environmental sampling, sediment and water handling, instrument calibration and maintenance, structured lab tasks, and data QA/QC procedures necessary to uphold USGS scientific standards.

This work includes frequent outdoor field duties in remote and sometimes harsh conditions (>50% during active sampling periods), complemented by periods of laboratory and office‑based data processing.

About the customer: The USGS conducts research to assess aquatic, hydrologic, and watershed conditions across the Kootenai and Clark Fork basins, supporting resource managers at the federal, state, Tribal, and local levels. These studies rely on accurate environmental measurements, properly maintained instruments, and high‑quality laboratory and data‑processing workflows to evaluate river conditions, sediment and water quality, and watershed responses to natural and anthropogenic stressors.

This Hybrid position requires that you live in Missoula, MT area and are able go to customer location in Bozeman, MT. if needed.

Responsibilities

The Physical Science Technician shall provide technical field support, environmental sample handling, instrument operation and maintenance, and data management services in accordance with USGS standard operating procedures, Quality Management Systems, and safety requirements.

The technician shall maintain accurate field logs, laboratory documentation, chain‑of‑custody materials, and metadata following Good Scientific Practices and USGS protocol expectations. The Physical Science Technician must be physically capable of walking on uneven terrain, wading streams, and lifting moderate loads in variable weather conditions.

Task 1. Field Data Collection & Instrument Support

Routine interaction with USGS scientists and technicians will be required to coordinate field schedules, address data or equipment issues, and ensure proper execution of study designs. Tasks to be performed are as follows:

Conduct field sampling of water, sediment, habitat, and related environmental parameters following USGS protocols.
Operate, calibrate, and maintain water‑quality sondes, flow meters, data loggers, autosamplers, and associated field instrumentation.
Record site conditions and measurements using clear, accurate metadata.
Support wading‑based or boat‑based sampling efforts as required.

Task 2. Laboratory Processing And Taxonomic Identification

Prepare, label, track, preserve, and transport environmental samples following chain‑of‑custody and QA/QC requirements.
Perform routine laboratory tasks including filtration, subsampling, drying, weighing, and workspace/equipment maintenance.
Prepare samples for shipment to analytical laboratories as directed.

Task 3. Data Management, Analysis, And Visualization

Enter field and laboratory data into project databases or spreadsheets.
Perform QA/QC to ensure completeness, consistency, and accuracy.
Produce basic figures, tables, and data summaries for internal use.
Maintain metadata and contribute to data documentation.

Task 4. Project Coordination & Technical Support

Assist with planning and preparation for field activities, including equipment staging and logistics.
Communicate data issues, equipment concerns, or irregularities to project supervisors.
Contribute to technical notes, field summaries, and report sections.
Participate in team meetings and coordination with partner agencies.

Qualifications

Must be a US Citizen able to pass a thorough background check including criminal and financial at both the state and federal level.
Bachelor Degree in a Science related discipline and 1 year of field sampling experience.
Strong analytical, problem-solving and computer skills.
Strong attention to detail.
The ability to use computer software and databases to develop complicated statistical and research reports.
Physical ability to work outdoors in remote settings, walk on uneven terrain, wade in streams, and lifting moderate loads in variable weather conditions.
Able to conduct occasional overnight fieldwork.

Travel

The primary base of operations shall be the USGS offices located on the University of Montana campus in Missoula, MT. Fieldwork may require overnight travel depending on sampling schedules and accessibility of field locations.

Physical Demands

Must be able to work extensively outdoors (>50%) in remote settings.
This includes walking on uneven terrain, wading streams, and lifting moderate loads in variable weather conditions.
Conduct occasional overnight fieldwork. Office work will be performed in a suitable office space (this includes a home office) or in an office at the principal duty station.

new_jobs.description:
ASE, an Akima company, is looking to hire a Physical Science Technician who will contribute to multidisciplinary research teams by supporting field data collection, maintaining scientific instrumentation, processing environmental samples, and organizing datasets used for hydrologic and watershed assessments. Work involves routine environmental sampling, sediment and water handling, instrument calibration and maintenance, structured lab tasks, and data QA/QC procedures necessary to uphold USGS scientific standards.

This work includes frequent outdoor field duties in remote and sometimes harsh conditions (>50% during active sampling periods), complemented by periods of laboratory and office‑based data processing.

About the customer: The USGS conducts research to assess aquatic, hydrologic, and watershed conditions across the Kootenai and Clark Fork basins, supporting resource managers at the federal, state, Tribal, and local levels. These studies rely on accurate environmental measurements, properly maintained instruments, and high‑quality laboratory and data‑processing workflows to evaluate river conditions, sediment and water quality, and watershed responses to natural and anthropogenic stressors.

This Hybrid position requires that you live in Missoula, MT area and are able go to customer location in Bozeman, MT. if needed.

Responsibilities

The Physical Science Technician shall provide technical field support, environmental sample handling, instrument operation and maintenance, and data management services in accordance with USGS standard operating procedures, Quality Management Systems, and safety requirements.

The technician shall maintain accurate field logs, laboratory documentation, chain‑of‑custody materials, and metadata following Good Scientific Practices and USGS protocol expectations. The Physical Science Technician must be physically capable of walking on uneven terrain, wading streams, and lifting moderate loads in variable weather conditions.

Task 1. Field Data Collection & Instrument Support

Routine interaction with USGS scientists and technicians will be required to coordinate field schedules, address data or equipment issues, and ensure proper execution of study designs. Tasks to be performed are as follows:

Conduct field sampling of water, sediment, habitat, and related environmental parameters following USGS protocols.
Operate, calibrate, and maintain water‑quality sondes, flow meters, data loggers, autosamplers, and associated field instrumentation.
Record site conditions and measurements using clear, accurate metadata.
Support wading‑based or boat‑based sampling efforts as required.

Task 2. Laboratory Processing And Taxonomic Identification

Prepare, label, track, preserve, and transport environmental samples following chain‑of‑custody and QA/QC requirements.
Perform routine laboratory tasks including filtration, subsampling, drying, weighing, and workspace/equipment maintenance.
Prepare samples for shipment to analytical laboratories as directed.

Task 3. Data Management, Analysis, And Visualization

Enter field and laboratory data into project databases or spreadsheets.
Perform QA/QC to ensure completeness, consistency, and accuracy.
Produce basic figures, tables, and data summaries for internal use.
Maintain metadata and contribute to data documentation.

Task 4. Project Coordination & Technical Support

Assist with planning and preparation for field activities, including equipment staging and logistics.
Communicate data issues, equipment concerns, or irregularities to project supervisors.
Contribute to technical notes, field summaries, and report sections.
Participate in team meetings and coordination with partner agencies.

Qualifications

Must be a US Citizen able to pass a thorough background check including criminal and financial at both the state and federal level.
Bachelor Degree in a Science related discipline and 1 year of field sampling experience.
Strong analytical, problem-solving and computer skills.
Strong attention to detail.
The ability to use computer software and databases to develop complicated statistical and research reports.
Physical ability to work outdoors in remote settings, walk on uneven terrain, wade in streams, and lifting moderate loads in variable weather conditions.
Able to conduct occasional overnight fieldwork.

Travel

The primary base of operations shall be the USGS offices located on the University of Montana campus in Missoula, MT. Fieldwork may require overnight travel depending on sampling schedules and accessibility of field locations.

Physical Demands

Must be able to work extensively outdoors (>50%) in remote settings.
This includes walking on uneven terrain, wading streams, and lifting moderate loads in variable weather conditions.
Conduct occasional overnight fieldwork. Office work will be performed in a suitable office space (this includes a home office) or in an office at the principal duty station.
